_comment: Per-clash deployment distance demo: the script's deployment_gap_m (60 m) is the same Battle.deployment_gap_m a campaign clash sets from its defended province's data, applied through BattleMap.with_line_gap. Team 0's line stays at y=300, team 1's line moves to y=1500 (1200 wu = 60 m below it, against the default 580 wu / 29 m), and the field grows downward to 1820 so the defenders keep their 320 wu of ground behind the line. Both armies therefore open BEYOND the 600-wu demote range: they start in the far tier (grid marks, no soldier bodies) and promote back to individual soldiers once the lines have closed inside 400 wu. Default 5v5 loadout on the default terrain, its own seed. The player's archers (x=642) and right-centre cavalry (x=1027) are box-selected and marched straight down the open lane between the forest (x 200-450) and the hill (x 1150-1400), so neither the forest's slow zone nor a detour around the hill muddies the march; the enemy AI advances to meet them. The clip shows the wide opening, the far-tier march, the promotion (around tick 900 for the archers and the enemy archers facing them), and the clash. The camera track matters here: the default whole-field camera sits at zoom 1.0, which shows 720 wu of a field whose lines are 1200 wu apart, so it frames neither line; a zoom-0.48 keyframe (1500 wu tall) held through tick 700 shows both far-tier lines and the whole march, then the track zooms to 1.0 on the clash by tick 1100. The spawn_fingerprint pins THIS widened layout, so a later re-spacing of the spawn table fails the recording loudly instead of letting the box-select land on empty ground.
